translation.document:
Six crucibles: 1 at the charging end, 6 at the tapping end. Melt counts in whole units. All start BASE.

Crucibles 1 to 6:
Working volume: 10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7
Upper mark: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5
Lower mark: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
Starting melt: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1
Line limit (all six): 38

Charges, crucibles 1 to 6:
Cycle 1: 0, 6, 3, 5, 3, 3
Cycle 2: 4, 2, 0, 1, 1, 7
Cycle 3: 4, 4, 3, 0, 0, 6
Cycle 4: 7, 6, 7, 1, 3, 0
Cycle 5: 0, 6, 6, 3, 3, 0

Five cycles, five steps each, in order. Finish each step on all six before the next.

1. Charge. Add the cycle's charge to each crucible. Volume isn't enforced; overfull is allowed.

2. Overflow. Work 1 to 6, one at a time. Anything above working volume runs down the launder into the next crucible, leaving this one exactly full. What comes from 1 lands in 2 before you check 2, so overflow can carry down the line. Overflow from 6 goes to the slag pit.

3. Temperature check, on contents after overflow. BASE at or above the upper mark goes SUPERHEATED. SUPERHEATED at or below the lower mark goes BASE. Between the marks, no change. At most one change per crucible per cycle. Log each as (cycle, position, before, after).

4. Tap. Work out all six amounts first, from current contents, rounded down: BASE gives a quarter, SUPERHEATED half. Then move them together. BASE melt goes to slag. SUPERHEATED melt runs up the return launder into the crucible before it; from crucible 1, to slag. Volume isn't enforced: overfill only runs off at the next cycle's overflow, so after cycle 5 it stays.

5. Emergency tap. Total all six. Over 38 (exactly 38 doesn't count), every crucible keeps half, rounded down; the rest goes to slag. Note the cycle.

Slag tally starts at zero: overflow from 6, BASE taps, crucible 1's SUPERHEATED tap, emergency taps.

Report. At the end of cycle 5, hand in: the six end quantities, positions 1 to 6; the six end states, same order; every state change as (cycle, position, before, after); the cycles the emergency tap fired; the slag tally; and the balance check: starting melt plus all charges must equal end melt plus slag tally.
reviewFixes: Cut the first draft from 482 words to 396, under the 400 cap, and kept every number: 6 working volumes, 6 upper marks, 6 lower marks, 6 starting amounts, the line limit and the 5x6 charge table.

Emergency tap: the draft said 'halve every crucible', which doesn't say which half gets rounded down. It now says each crucible keeps half, rounded down, which matches the process (keep floor(level/2), the remainder goes to slag).
Tap step: said that all six amounts are rounded down and are worked out from the contents before anything moves.
Made the threshold explicit: the emergency tap fires only when the total is strictly over 38, and exactly 38 does not fire it.
Said that capacity is not enforced at charging or at the tap step, that overfill runs off only at the next cycle's overflow, and that overfill left after cycle 5 stays in the end figures.
Added that each state change happens at most once per crucible per cycle, and that a crucible between the marks keeps its state.
Listed every route into the slag tally (overflow from crucible 6, BASE taps, crucible 1's SUPERHEATED tap, emergency taps) so the balance check can close.
Removed the hyphenated term 'spill-over' and checked the final text against the banned-word list; none of the banned words appear.
Kept the Report paragraph to a template only, with no figures or results.

translation.document:
Six crucibles: 1 at the charging end, 6 at the tapping end. Melt counts in whole units.

Crucible: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
Working volume: 10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7
Upper mark: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5
Lower mark: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
Starting melt: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1

All start BASE. The slag tally starts at zero and counts everything sent to slag. Emergency tap limit, whole line: 38.

Five cycles, five steps each, in this order; each step finishes on all six before the next starts.

1. Charge. Add the cycle's charge from the table (positions 1 to 6). A crucible can stand over working volume here.

Cycle 1: 0, 6, 3, 5, 3, 3
Cycle 2: 4, 2, 0, 1, 1, 7
Cycle 3: 4, 4, 3, 0, 0, 6
Cycle 4: 7, 6, 7, 1, 3, 0
Cycle 5: 0, 6, 6, 3, 3, 0

2. Overflow. One crucible at a time, 1 through 6: anything above working volume runs down the launder into the next crucible, leaving this one exactly full. Overflow from 6 goes to the slag pit. Overflow from upstream arrives before you check a crucible, so it can cascade down the line.

3. State check, after overflow. BASE at or above the upper mark goes SUPERHEATED. SUPERHEATED at or below the lower mark returns to BASE. Between the marks, no change. At most one change per crucible per cycle. Log each as (cycle, position, before, after).

4. Draw-down. Figure all six amounts from current melt before moving anything. BASE gives a quarter, rounded down, to slag. SUPERHEATED sends half, rounded down, up the return launder into the crucible before it; crucible 1's half goes to slag. Then move all six at once. Returned melt can leave a crucible over working volume until the next cycle's overflow; after cycle 5 it stays over.

5. Emergency tap. Total the six. Strictly over 38: every crucible keeps half, rounded down, the rest to slag; note the cycle. At 38 or under, nothing.

Report. At the end of cycle 5 hand in: the six end quantities, positions 1 to 6; the six end states, same order; every state change as (cycle, position, before, after); the cycles the emergency tap fired; the slag tally; and the balance check: starting melt plus all charges equals end melt plus slag tally.
reviewFixes: The first draft was 517 words. I cut it to 399 (checked with wc -w) and kept every number: the six working volumes, six upper marks, six lower marks, six starting amounts, the limit of 38 and the 5-by-6 charge table.
The emergency tap is now 'every crucible keeps half, rounded down, the rest to slag'. This matches floor(level/2) exactly, with the larger half going to slag, and avoids an ambiguous 'halve'.
The tap trigger now says 'strictly over 38', with 'At 38 or under, nothing'. This makes clear that a total of exactly 38 does not fire it.
In the overflow step, 'leaving it exactly full' became 'leaving this one exactly full'. 'It' could have meant the receiving crucible.

The vague 'overflow reaching a crucible before you check it counts' became 'overflow from upstream arrives before you check a crucible, so it can cascade down the line'. This states the 1-to-6 cascade within one pass.
The bare 'Line limit: 38' became 'Emergency tap limit, whole line: 38', so the number is tied to the step that uses it.

The slag tally is now stated as starting at zero and counting everything sent to slag. This covers all three routes: overflow from crucible 6, BASE draw-down plus crucible 1's SUPERHEATED half, and the emergency tap.
I added that draw-down amounts are worked out from current melt before anything moves, and that all six moves happen at once.
I added that working volume is not enforced after charging or draw-down. An overfull crucible is cleared only at the next cycle's overflow and stays over after cycle 5.

I removed every banned word and checked by regex for cell, level, mode, period, intake, spill, release, lost and the rest. This included replacing the draft wording for the fourth step with 'Draw-down'.
I confirmed that the Report paragraph is a template only, with no figures or results, and that it asks for the balance check as starting melt plus all charges equals end melt plus slag tally.

translation.document:
Six chambers in a row: chamber 1 at the head, 6 at the tail. Each holds a whole number of units of nutrient mass, never negative. All start LARVAL; loss tally starts at 0.

Chambers 1 to 6:
Capacity: 10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7
Upper mark: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5
Lower mark: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
Starting mass: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1
Moult limit, whole line: 38

A run is five cycles, five steps each, in this order. Finish each step on all six before the next.

1. Feed. Add the cycle's ration from the feed table. Capacity ignored here.

2. Overflow. Walk 1 to 6. Anything over capacity moves into the next chamber, leaving it exactly at capacity. Chamber 1's excess reaches 2 before you check 2, so it cascades. Chamber 6's excess goes to the loss tally.

3. State check, on post-overflow mass. LARVAL at or above its upper mark goes PUPAL. PUPAL at or below its lower mark returns to LARVAL; that's routine. Between marks, state holds. At most one change per chamber per cycle; log each.

4. Metabolism. Work out all six amounts from mass at the start of this step before touching anything: LARVAL, a quarter; PUPAL, half; both rounded down. Apply together. Each chamber gives up its amount. LARVAL amounts are metabolised away to the loss tally. PUPAL amounts are reabsorbed into the chamber before it (4 sends to 3); chamber 1's PUPAL amount goes to the loss tally. No capacity check: an overfull chamber waits for next cycle's overflow; after cycle 5, it stays over.

5. Moult. If the six chambers total strictly more than 38, every chamber halves, rounded down; removed mass goes to the loss tally; note the cycle. At 38 or under, nothing.

Feed table, chambers 1 to 6:
Cycle 1: 0, 6, 3, 5, 3, 3
Cycle 2: 4, 2, 0, 1, 1, 7
Cycle 3: 4, 4, 3, 0, 0, 6
Cycle 4: 7, 6, 7, 1, 3, 0
Cycle 5: 0, 6, 6, 3, 3, 0

Report. After cycle 5, hand in: the six end masses in order 1 to 6; the six end states, same order; every state change as (cycle, chamber, before, after); the cycles the moult fired; the loss tally; and the balance check: starting total plus all feed must equal end total plus loss tally.
reviewFixes: Cut the first draft from 513 words to 399 (counted with wc -w) to get under the 400-word cap, keeping every rule and number.
Labelled the feed table's columns as chambers 1 to 6, because the trim had left it unclear which number belonged to which chamber.
Added that each chamber's mass is a whole number and never negative, which the first outline left out.
Said outright that a chamber between its two marks keeps the state it already has, and that each chamber changes state at most once per cycle and every change is logged.
Made the metabolism step say that all six amounts are worked out from the mass at the start of the step before anything is applied, and that every chamber, LARVAL or PUPAL, gives up its own amount.

Covered the edge cases: a PUPAL chamber 1 sends its reabsorbed amount to the loss tally, and a chamber overfilled during metabolism is only corrected at the next cycle's overflow, so after cycle 5 it stays over capacity.
Specified that the moult fires only when the total is strictly over 38 (nothing happens at 38 or under), that halving rounds down, and that the cycle gets noted.
Wrote the overflow cascade (chamber 1's excess reaching chamber 2 before chamber 2 is checked) and chamber 6's excess going to the loss tally.
Ran a search for every banned word (including 'lost', 'level' and 'period') and found none; removed the numbered-position shorthand 'n-1' in favour of the example '4 sends to 3'.
Checked that the Report paragraph is only a template, with no figures, totals or results.

translation.document:
Six rearing chambers run in a row, chamber 1 first, chamber 6 last. Mass is counted in whole nutrient units. Each chamber is LARVAL or PUPAL; all start LARVAL. Keep a loss tally from 0: everything discarded or metabolised goes on it.

Chambers 1 to 6:
Holding limit: 10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7
Upper mark: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5
Lower mark: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
Starting mass: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1
Moult threshold, whole line: 38

Feed per cycle, chambers 1 to 6:
Cycle 1: 0, 6, 3, 5, 3, 3
Cycle 2: 4, 2, 0, 1, 1, 7
Cycle 3: 4, 4, 3, 0, 0, 6
Cycle 4: 7, 6, 7, 1, 3, 0
Cycle 5: 0, 6, 6, 3, 3, 0

Five cycles, five steps each, always in this order; finish each step on all six chambers before the next.

1. Feed. Add each chamber's table amount. No trimming; chambers may sit over limit.

2. Carry forward. Go chamber 1, 2, through 6. Anything above a chamber's limit moves into the next chamber, leaving it exactly at its limit. Chamber 1's excess reaches chamber 2 before chamber 2 is checked, so excess can cascade. Chamber 6's excess is discarded.

3. State check, on post-carry mass. LARVAL at or above its upper mark goes PUPAL. PUPAL at or below its lower mark returns to LARVAL, which is routine. Between marks, state holds. At most one change per chamber per cycle. Log each as (cycle, position, before, after).

4. Metabolism. First work out all six amounts from current contents, before changing any: LARVAL loses a quarter, PUPAL half, each rounded down. Then apply them together. LARVAL amounts are metabolised away. PUPAL amounts are reabsorbed into the previous chamber; chamber 1's, if PUPAL, is discarded. No limit applies here; overfull chambers are corrected only at the next cycle's carry forward, never after cycle 5.

5. Moult. Total the six chambers. Strictly above 38: every chamber keeps half, rounded down, the rest discarded; note the cycle. At 38 or below, nothing.

Report. After cycle 5, hand in: the six end quantities, positions 1 to 6; the six end states, same order; every state change as (cycle, position, before, after); the cycles the moult fired; the loss tally; and the balance check: starting quantities plus all feed must equal end quantities plus the loss tally.
reviewFixes: The first draft was 555 words, over the 400-word cap. I cut it to 399 (counted with wc -w, numbers included) without losing any steps or numbers.
Added 'strictly' and 'At 38 or below, nothing' so the moult clearly does not fire at exactly 38.
Made the metabolism rule say that all six amounts are worked out from current contents before any chamber changes, and that each amount is rounded down.
Made clear that the moult keeps half of each chamber rounded down, so the part discarded is the rest (the larger half when the mass is odd).
Said that chamber 1's amount goes on the tally when chamber 1 is PUPAL, since there is no chamber before it.
Said that capacity is not enforced at feeding or metabolism, that an overfull chamber is only corrected at the next cycle's carry forward, and that after cycle 5 it is never corrected.
Spelled out that carry forward can cascade: chamber 1's excess reaches chamber 2 before chamber 2 is checked.
Added that the state check uses the mass after carry forward, that a chamber between its marks keeps its state, and that a chamber changes state at most once per cycle.
Defined the loss tally at the start as everything discarded or metabolised, so every later 'discarded' clearly goes on it.
Replaced the banned words 'spill-over', 'release' and 'intake' with carry forward, metabolism and feed. Checked the text with grep: none of the banned words remain.
Kept the Report paragraph as a template only, with no figures; the balance check is given as a formula.

run.procedureSummary: I ran 5 cycles with 5 steps each and finished every step on all six crucibles before starting the next. (1) Charge: I added the cycle's charge to each crucible, with no volume cap. (2) Overflow: working from crucible 1 to 6, any amount above working volume went into the next crucible, which was checked only after receiving it. Overflow from crucible 6 went to slag. (3) Temperature check on the contents after overflow: BASE at or above the upper mark became SUPERHEATED, and SUPERHEATED at or below the lower mark became BASE. Each crucible was checked once per cycle, so it could change at most once. (4) Tap: all six amounts were worked out first from the post-check contents and states, rounded down (BASE floor(q/4), SUPERHEATED floor(q/2)), then moved together. BASE taps went to slag. A SUPERHEATED tap went to crucible i-1, except crucible 1's, which went to slag. Volume was not enforced. (5) Emergency tap: if the line total after tapping was over 38 (strictly), each crucible kept floor(q/2) and the remainder went to slag.

openPoints.point: Which contents and states the tap amounts use
openPoints.assumption: Contents after overflow, with the states as they stand after that cycle's temperature check.

openPoints.point: When the emergency total is taken
openPoints.assumption: After the step-4 tap moves are complete, including the melt returned up the return launder.

openPoints.point: At most one state change per crucible per cycle
openPoints.assumption: The temperature check runs once per crucible per cycle, so the rule is met automatically. A crucible can change state only in step 3.

openPoints.point: Rounding in the emergency halving
openPoints.assumption: Each crucible keeps floor(q/2). The amount removed (q - floor(q/2)), including the odd unit, goes to slag.

openPoints.point: Overfill after the cycle 5 tap
openPoints.assumption: It stays, as the write-up says. Crucible 2 ends at 10 against a volume of 8, and crucible 4 at 7 against 6.

openPoints.point: Temperature check on an exact mark
openPoints.assumption: Taken as written: 'at or above upper' and 'at or below lower' include the marks themselves.

openPoints.point: At most one state change per cycle

run.procedureSummary:
Five cycles. Each cycle runs these steps in order, and every step finishes on all six crucibles before the next one starts.
(1) Charge: add the cycle's charge to each crucible. Capacity is not enforced at this step.
(2) Overflow: go through crucibles 1 to 6 in order. Any amount above working volume moves to the next crucible, so it is included when that crucible is checked. Overflow from crucible 6 goes to slag.
(3) Temperature check, using contents after overflow: BASE at or above the upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED. SUPERHEATED at or below the lower mark becomes BASE. Each crucible is checked once per cycle, so it changes at most once.
(4) Tap: calculate all six amounts from the contents before any tap moves. BASE taps floor(q/4) and SUPERHEATED taps floor(q/2). Then move them all at once. BASE taps go to slag. A SUPERHEATED tap goes to the crucible before it (position i-1), except crucible 1's, which goes to slag. Overfill is allowed.
(5) Emergency tap: if the line total after tapping is above 38, every crucible keeps floor(q/2) and the rest goes to slag. A total of exactly 38 does not fire it.
The slag tally adds overflow from crucible 6, BASE taps, crucible 1's SUPERHEATED taps and emergency removals.

openPoints.point: Rounding of the emergency halving
openPoints.assumption: Each crucible keeps floor(q/2) separately. The remainder, including any odd unit, goes to slag.

openPoints.point: Which state decides a crucible's tap fraction

openPoints.point: Whether returned melt can trigger a second state change

openPoints.point: Crucibles over volume after the cycle 5 tap
openPoints.assumption: They stay overfull, as the write-up says (crucible 2 ends at 10 against a volume of 8). No extra overflow pass is run.

openPoints.point: Order in which taps are applied
openPoints.assumption: All amounts are calculated from the same snapshot of contents, then moved together, so the order of moves does not change the result.

run.procedureSummary: Five cycles of five steps, each step finished on all six crucibles before the next starts. (1) Charge: add the cycle's charge to each position. Melt may stand over working volume. (2) Overflow: go through positions 1 to 6 in order. Any melt above working volume moves to the next crucible and the crucible is left exactly at working volume.
